errors.why_wrong: This ovarian axis uses pulsatile GnRH. TRH primarily regulates thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), so this label teaches the wrong hypothalamic signal. [Endotext](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK279070/)

errors.what: “TSH and ACTH” on the pituitary-to-ovary arrow
errors.why_wrong: The anterior pituitary signals the ovary through LH and FSH, not TSH or ACTH. [Endotext](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK279070/)

errors.what: The solid estradiol feedback arrows and “(positive at mid-cycle: LH surge)”
errors.why_wrong: The same arrows depict both negative feedback and the mid-cycle positive switch without showing which effect applies when. The distinction is left entirely to the label.

errors.what: The dashed inhibin arrow ends at the undifferentiated “Anterior pituitary” box
errors.why_wrong: Although the nearby text says inhibin suppresses FSH only, the diagram does not identify an FSH output or show its selective suppression.

errors.what: Small diagram labels and low-contrast brown text
errors.why_wrong: The labels are readable at the supplied size but require effort; no text appears clipped or overlapping.

verdict: The caption describes the ovarian axis correctly, but the diagram labels its two central hormone pathways with hormones from other endocrine axes.
